title: The Moon Never Rushes Its Phases
core_idea: The moon's cycles mirror human seasons of fullness and retreat; neither phase is a failure.
text: The moon is never in a hurry to be full. Night after night, it grows a little, then softens, then disappears for a while, and then begins again. No one calls the new moon a failure. It's simply part of the cycle. Many traditions have looked to the moon as a mirror for our inner lives. Times to shine, and times to rest in the dark. Perhaps you're in a quieter phase right now, giving less light than you'd like. That's not falling behind. It may be the very rhythm that prepares you for fullness again. Tonight, if the sky is clear, look up and let the moon remind you.
description: A reflection on the moon's phases as a mirror for our own seasons of fullness and rest.
